tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description:
The TofuBofu workspaces you can reach, each with its plan, your role, the
    brands (websites) it measures, and whether its plan includes working the
    account from here. Most accounts have one. The `default` workspace is the
    one picked when TofuBofu was connected.

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description:
Your scans, newest first, with their status and report link. Read one
    with get_visibility_report.

tools.name: get_latest_summary
tools.description:
The latest finished scan for a brand: the Tofu Index and the Bofu Index,
    each with its fraction, the Tofu Index per engine, who AI names instead,
    and the top open items of the Fixes list, plus the report link. The same shape as
    get_visibility_report.

tools.name: get_fixes
tools.description:
The brand's Fixes list: the one-time technical, schema and listing fixes
    that make the site readable and citable by AI engines, highest impact
    first, each found by our own crawl and scan. The same list as the Fixes page.
    Work through them with the user, then call mark_fix when one is don

tools.name: mark_fix
tools.description:
Record that the user did a fix (or reopen one). Only on the user's word
    that it is done: the next scan re-checks it and the Fixes page shows it.

tools.name: list_queries
tools.description:
Every buying query in the latest scan: which engines named the brand,
    which answered without naming it, and the firms they named instead. A query
    here is one question; each engine's answer to it is counted separately in
    the Tofu Index. Read an engine's full answer with get_query_answers.

tools.name: get_query_answers
tools.description:
Each engine's full answer to one buying query in the latest scan, with
    whether it named the brand and which firms it named. Use it to see why an
    engine picks a rival and what a page would have to say to change that.

tools.name: get_analyst_context
tools.description:
Everything the TofuBofu Agent reads before answering: the last six
    scans and their trend, every query with its movement, competitors, the
    strategic read, the content pipeline, fixes and AI referral traffic, as one
    plain-text pack. Read it once, then answer the user's questions from it.

tools.name: list_content
tools.description:
The Content Engine's pieces for this brand (blog posts, video scripts,
    newsletters): each one's status and the buying queries it targets. Read one
    with get_content_piece.

tools.name: get_content_piece
tools.description:
One Content Engine piece: its title, the buying queries it targets, its
    status, and the draft once written (markdown, meta description, FAQ).

Returns a score out of 50, the band it falls in against a measured sampl

tools.name: check_ai_slop
tools.description: Check a piece of writing for the habits that make it read as machine-written: stock phrases, em dashes, rigid sentence shapes. Returns a score out of 50 against the floor TofuBofu holds its own copy to, the phrases flagged and where. Use it on a draft before it is published. Pass the text itself.

tools.name: grade_content_for_aeo
tools.description: Grade a draft or a live page as content an AI engine can cite: structure, directness, evidence and readability, with the changes that raise it. Needs at least 150 words of text, or a page URL. Use it when someone asks whether an article is good enough to rank or be cited, or wants an AEO pass over c

tools.name: check_stats_and_sources
tools.description: Find every statistic in a draft and check whether each one has a source link beside it and whether the link works and says what the draft says it does. Flags unsourced, dead-sourced and misquoted figures. Use it before publishing anything that quotes a number. Pass the text of the draft.

tools.name: ask_ai_engines
tools.description: Ask one buyer query to every AI engine TofuBofu tracks (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Mode) live, with web search on, and see which companies each engine names, which pages it cites and the searches it ran. Use it to learn who an engine recommends for a query, what a competitor i

tools.description: Call this first, before any other TofuBofu tool. It says whether the person is signed in to a TofuBofu account, what their plan includes and exactly what to do next: the free scan for someone new, or the account tools (brand brief, content briefs, draft checks) for a customer. tools.name: get_brand_brief
tools.description: Who this company is, so a piece sounds like them: the market and goals they told TofuBofu, the voice guide, the rivals being tracked and the pages their site already has, so a new piece does not repeat one. Read it once per writing session, before list_content_briefs.

tools.name: list_content_briefs
tools.description: The article briefs TofuBofu has queued for this brand, each from a buying query where AI engines name someone else. Every brief says which query it targets, the page type engines cite for it and who they name instead. Pick one, then call get_content_brief.

tools.name: get_content_brief
tools.description: Everything TofuBofu's own writer reads for one brief: the page type and shape that wins the query, the sources and facts you may use, the links you may use, the writing rules and what this customer told us. Write the piece from it, run check_draft until it passes, then submit_draft.

tools.name: check_draft
tools.description: Check a draft against its brief before saving it: the writing score, banned phrases, em dashes, claims about TofuBofu's own measurement or about what AI assistants answer, the shape the brief asks for and links outside the allowed list. Returns pass, or the exact edits to make. Saves nothing and cha

tools.name: submit_draft
tools.description: Save a draft that passed check_draft onto its brief, as a draft in the customer's Content Engine. A draft that fails the same checks is refused with the exact edits to make. It does not publish: the customer reviews and approves it in the Content Engine, and that tap is theirs.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: scan_ai_visibility, list_content, score_page_citability · Private data: scan_ai_visibility, mark_fix, generate_llms_txt · Public sink: scan_ai_visibility, get_visibility_report, get_competitors, submit_draft · Destructive: audit_site_for_ai, generate_llms_txt, get_content_brief.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: scan_ai_visibility, list_content, score_page_citability · Private data: scan_ai_visibility, mark_fix, generate_llms_txt · Public sink: scan_ai_visibility, get_visibility_report, get_competitors, submit_draft · Destructive: audit_site_for_ai, generate_llms_txt, get_content_brief

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
